title: Operationalisation Laboratory
summary: Build a measurement plan for academic engagement from four candidate measures and watch two consequences move at once: how much of the construct the plan reaches, facet by facet, and how much of what it records is not the construct at all. Adding measures to close one gap widens the other.
learningObjectives: Explain why an operational definition is a claim about the construct rather than a translation of it.
Distinguish construct under-representation from construct-irrelevant variance, and identify each in a specific measurement plan.
Predict how adding a measure changes coverage and contamination, and recognise that the two move in opposite directions.
Explain why coverage is the best any single measure achieves rather than the sum across measures.
Recognise that combining measures buys coverage without buying the construct, and that some facets may stay out of reach entirely.
interactionTypes: live coverage map recomputed on every change
measurement plan built by toggling measures on and off
facet-level bar readout paired with a word for each level
construct-irrelevant variance listed live beside the plan
explanation withheld until the learner has changed the plan
privacy: Nothing is collected, stored or transmitted. All processing happens in the browser and no selections persist after the page is closed.
accessibilityNotes: Keyboard operable throughout. Each measure is a full-width label containing a native checkbox, so the whole row is the target and the tick is a non-colour state signal; the focus ring is drawn around the row rather than the box. Every facet bar is paired with a word - not reached, partly reached, well reached - so no level depends on reading a bar length or a colour. Coverage and unreached-facet counts are announced through a polite live region on every change. The facet definitions are given as text beneath the map. No timed content and no motion.
dataStatus: Fictional teaching material. The four measures are described generically; no published instrument, item or proprietary assessment is reproduced, and no figures from any real study are used.
simulationNotes: The five facets are a teaching model, not a fact: other accounts of engagement use three facets or four, and some argue engagement is a property of a situation rather than of a student. Each measure carries a coverage level per facet of 0, 1 or 2, and a plan's level for a facet is the maximum across selected measures rather than the sum - two partial views of a facet are not one good measure of it. The coverage figure is arithmetic over that facet list, out of 10. It is not a validity coefficient and must not be read as one. The agentic facet is reached at best partly by any measure here, so no plan can exceed 9 of 10; that ceiling is deliberate and carried over from the original.
readmeTopic: operationalisation, construct coverage and the trade-off between under-representation and irrelevant variance
